newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices fall in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices fall in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices eased at this week's sales, particularly on the last day's sales in Sydney and Melbourne, Wesfarmers Dalgety said in its weekly report.
The eastern market indicator fell 18 cents to 660 cents a kilogram clean over the week.
Wesfarmers said the anticipated dampening effect of larger rostered quantities came to fruition this week to a greater extent than many in the trade expected.
"Following the 10 percent market rise throughout April, buyers were waiting for prices to establish more realistic levels in order to generate new orders," Wesfarmers said.
A total of 71,236 bales were offered at auction with a pass in rate of 11.9 percent.
Wool International stockpile totalled 1,708,593. Trade competition was led by Japanese and Chinese buyers with support from Western European and Taiwanese buyers.
In the futures market a total of 212 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract for the week ending May 8.
Open interest increased by 53 contracts to close at 918.
The June 1997 contract closed 18 cents down at 788 cents kg clean.
The August 19976 contract closed 21 cents down at 777 cents a kg clean.
Sales next week are in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle with 110,568 bales rostered for sale.
